thread.title: Tech Stocks Rally As Apple, Intel Boost Dow, But Bitcoin Dives

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Tech Stocks Rally As Apple, Intel Boost Dow, But Bitcoin Dives
text:
Key market index funds posted solid gains Thursday as Apple ( AAPL ), Intel ( INTC ) and other tech stocks took part in the rally.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) advanced 1.3% each while PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) rallied 1.8% in the stock market today . Emerging markets also outperformed as iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM ) soared 2.1%.
Metals miners, energy and semiconductors were among top sector fund gainers. SPDR S&P Metals & Mining ( XME ) leapt 3% after finding support at its 200-day moving average. VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) rose 2.1% as it tries to work its way back to its 50-day line, which sits 2% ahead.
Graphics chip designer Nvidia ( NVDA ) surged 4.6% and Dow component Intel vaulted 5%. Also among blue chips, Apple rose as much as 3% before trimming its gain to less than 1%. The iPhone maker briefly reclaimed its 50-day line before easing. Shares are 2% below their 50-day and 8% off their high. Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Cisco ( CSCO ) were also advanced on the Dow, up a respective 2.1% and 3%.
Technology Select Sector SPDR ( XLK ) recovered 2% as Facebook ( FB ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) also rebounded. Facebook popped 4%; Alphabet retook its 200-day line with a 3.1% advance.
Bitcoin slumped 8% to $7,270.51, according to CoinDesk , after getting near $8,000 earlier. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) gapped down and lost 7% to extend its losing streak for a sixth straight session. It breached its 200-day line Wednesday. Two Japanese cryptocurrency exchanges will reportedly shut down over regulatory compliance.
Gold Shines Finding stock funds near buy points is a tough feat as market volatility continues. But gold plays are looking more attractive, by comparison.
SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) fell below its 50-day moving average Wednesday. It hasn't strayed too far from the support line during the past month and may be shaping a flat base with a potential buy point at 129.61. The fund was last featured in this ETF column on March 1 as it tested its 50-day moving average, before breaching it the next session.
The $36.5 billion fund, which marked its 13th anniversary in November, tracks the price of gold bullion. Its year-to-date return of 1.7% through Wednesday, according to Morningstar Inc., outpaces the S&P 500's 1.8% loss. Over the longer haul, though, the metal ETF's returns lag the S&P index by a wide margin. It carries a 0.40% expense ratio.
Smaller and younger peer iShares Gold Trust ( IAU ) is tracing a similar pattern. The possible buy point for IAU is 13.21. The $11.7 billion fund, which turned 13 years old in January, was also featured in the March 1 column. IAU returned 1.8% year-to-date as of Wednesday.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Frank Holmes, chief executive officer of U.S. Global Investors, thinks gold prices could rise to as high as $1,500 this year. In a Monday blog post , he said he stands by that forecast, which he initially made in January.
"Before last week, investors might have been slightly disappointed by gold's mostly sideways performance so far this year," he wrote. "But now, in response to a number of factors, it's up close to 3% in 2018, compared to the S&P 500 index, down 2.4%."
In January, he said there could be another "Fed rally" this year following the December rate hike. If gold sees similar gains as the past two cycles, its price could go up to $1,500. Holmes also cited recent market volatility and President Trump's appointment of a new chief economic advisor as potential catalysts.
